decisions.reason: As a recent flagship electrometer tightly tied to the firm's core radiation-therapy QA business and previously highlighted prominently, it is very unlikely to be withdrawn so soon.

The oncology risk-management software extends the firm's established QA and workflow portfolio and fits an expanding, innovation-led business, so continued development is more likely than discontinuation.
This CT image-quality phantom builds directly on the firm's medical-imaging QA capabilities, making it a natural portfolio extension that management would usually keep on the market.

Although the mammography image-quality phantom is somewhat more distant from the firm's traditional radiation-therapy focus, it still fits adjacent imaging QA needs and is too new to remove quickly unless demand disappoints.

The full-field mammography test phantom is also peripheral to the firm's strongest core and may face a narrower market, but as a newly launched adjacent QA product it is still more likely to be retained than dropped.
A newly launched medical-imaging QA instrument line presented as a strategic focus is likely to receive ongoing commercial and technical support rather than be taken off the market within a year.
